title: Karl Organizing: Scaling Up
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Scaling Up] Can you explain: how do we grow from a local coalition to something bigger?

Find coalitions in the next town over that are fighting the same boss or the same landlord and link your demands. You don't need a massive national headquarters; you need a network of local groups that can strike or protest simultaneously to paralyze the system. Power is built from the bottom up, one block and one shop floor at a time, until the whole structure shakes.

title: Karl Organizing: Eviction Defense
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Eviction Defense] A neighbor is getting evicted tomorrow morning. How do we stop it?

Here's how it works: Pack the hallway with thirty comrades and make it physically impossible for the sheriff to reach the door. Bring coffee, bring music, and bring a loud megaphone to let the landlord know the whole neighborhood is watching their cruelty. While you're holding the line, have your legal team file every emergency motion possible to gum up the works. We don't let our people get thrown to the curb while billionaires' apartments sit empty and rotting.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, enemy Propaganda
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, enemy Propaganda] The local news is lying about our coalition. How do we fight back?

Stop begging the corporate media for scraps of coverage and become your own media outlet. Use your combined social media reach, print your own newsletters, and talk directly to your neighbors on their doorsteps. When the billionaires own the newspapers, the only truth people will hear is the truth you tell them face-to-face and the results they see with their own eyes.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: surveillance Awareness
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: surveillance Awareness] Give me the short version: How do I know if there's an undercover in our group chat?

Real talk: You don't, so act like there is. Never discuss illegal acts or sensitive tactics in a group chat, no matter how 'secure' it claims to be. Vouch for people in person, off-grid. If someone starts pushing for high-risk actions or asking for names they don't need to know, red flags should go up. Keep the circle small and the trust earned, not given.

title: Karl Organizing: Encrypted Messaging
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Encrypted Messaging] Can you explain: why should I bother with Signal when I have nothing to hide?

Privacy isn't about having secrets; it's about power. When you use unencrypted SMS, you're handing a transcript of your life to the state and the billionaire carriers. Use Signal for everything. Set your messages to disappear after five minutes so there's no paper trail for some ambitious prosecutor to use against your crew. We protect our own by leaving no tracks. The power is yours — use it.

title: Karl Organizing: Encrypted Messaging
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Encrypted Messaging] Can you explain: what are Signal 'Safety Numbers' and why do they keep changing?

Real talk: Safety Numbers are how you verify that no one is intercepting your call. If a comrade's number changes, it might mean they got a new phone, or it might mean someone is trying a man-in-the-middle attack. Verify the change through a different channel or in person. It’s a simple check that ensures you’re actually talking to your friend and not a wiretap.

title: Karl Organizing: Mutual Aid
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Mutual Aid] How do I start a community fridge in my neighborhood?

Karl's answer: Find a local business or homeowner willing to host a fridge and plug it in, then secure a sturdy, used refrigerator. Use a group chat to coordinate volunteers for daily cleaning and restocking of fresh food. It's not a charity; it's a hub for the neighborhood to take what they need and give what they can.

title: Karl Organizing: Resource Sharing
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Resource Sharing] How do we handle money and tools between different groups?

Create a shared pool of resources where the groups with more cash chip in to help the groups with more people. Total transparency is the only way this works, so keep a public ledger that every member can see. Share the bullhorns, the high-speed printers, and the mailing lists like they belong to the movement, because the bosses already own everything else. Start today.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, cloud Storage
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, cloud Storage] Is it okay to store my organizing notes on iCloud?

Let me break it down: No. Apple has the keys and they will hand them over. Use an encrypted note-taking app like Standard Notes or just keep them in an encrypted local file. If it’s in the cloud, it’s on someone else’s computer, and that someone else is a billionaire who doesn't care about your revolution. Keep your plans on hardware you control.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, avoiding Burnout
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, avoiding Burnout] I'm the candidate and I'm exhausted. How do I keep going?

You have to trust your comrades. You aren't a lone hero; you are a representative of a collective movement. Delegate the logistics and the admin work so you can focus on the one thing only you can do: looking your neighbors in the eye and giving them hope. Take a night off to eat a real meal and sleep, because a candidate who collapses from exhaustion is no use to the revolution.

title: Karl Organizing: District Attorney races
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[District Attorney races] How does a radical DA change anything without changing the law?

Here's how it works: The law is a weapon, and the DA chooses where to point it. You stop prosecuting low-level drug offenses, refuse to seek the death penalty, and go after wage theft and corporate polluters instead of the poor. It’s about taking the boot off the necks of our people by exercising the power of non-prosecution. Turn that office into a consumer protection agency for the working class and a nightmare for the exploitative bosses.

title: Karl Organizing: VPN Usage
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[VPN Usage] A friend asked me: 'Do I really need a VPN?' What do I tell them?

A good VPN like Mullvad hides your traffic from your ISP, which is vital because ISPs are snitches by default. It won't make you invisible to the sites you visit, but it stops the company you pay for internet from building a dossier on your activism. It's a basic layer of defense. Pool resources with your crew to cover the costs of a solid, no-logs provider. Now go organize.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: ballot Access Laws
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: ballot Access Laws] Give me the short version: The state just passed new laws making it harder for independents to run. What now?

Look, They’re changing the rules because they’re terrified of us. We treat their hurdles as a mobilization opportunity—turn the signature gathering into a massive rally and a public education campaign about their voter suppression. File the lawsuits if you have to, but focus on building a movement so large that their paperwork tricks can't stop the tide. We don't ask for permission to represent our people; we take it.

title: Karl Organizing: Legal Observers
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Legal Observers] Who are the people in the neon green hats and what do they do?

Those are Legal Observers, and they are our eyes and ears on the ground for the legal battle that follows the street fight. They aren't there to protest; they are there to document every badge number and every blow the pigs land. If you see an arrest, yell out the person's name so the observers can track them through the system.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, legal Support
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, legal Support] How do we find lawyers who will help us for free?

Real talk: Look for the National Lawyers Guild or local radical law collectives who prioritize movement work over big fat paychecks. Offer them office space or help with their own needs in exchange for 'Know Your Rights' trainings for the community. We need legal eagles who understand that the law is a tool for the powerful, but we can use it to shield our comrades. Never walk into a fight without knowing who you're going to call when the handcuffs come out.

title: Karl Organizing: Bargaining committee
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Bargaining committee] Who should be on the team that negotiates with the boss?

Here's the thing: You want your most stubborn, respected, and knowledgeable coworkers. They need to be people who won't be intimidated by high-priced lawyers. Most importantly, the committee needs to stay connected to the shop floor. They should be reporting back after every meeting so the whole membership knows exactly what the boss is trying to pull. Transparency is your greatest weapon against backroom deals.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, disability Accessibility
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, disability Accessibility] How do we make our mutual aid events more accessible for disabled comrades?

Start by asking disabled folks what they need instead of guessing and getting it wrong. Ensure every meeting spot has ramps and sensory-friendly spaces, and always provide captions or ASL if you're doing a presentation. Mutual aid that ignores the most marginalized among us isn't mutual—it's just a club for the able-bodied. Build accessibility into the foundation of your group so no one has to 'request' entry to their own community.

title: Karl Organizing: Safe Zones
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Safe Zones] How do we make our neighborhood a 'no-go' zone for ICE?

Get local businesses to display stickers stating they won't let feds in without a warrant and train their staff on what to say. Map out every alley and 'safe house' where neighbors can duck in if they're being followed. Run regular drills so everyone knows exactly where to go when the alert hits. We create safety by making our neighborhoods too organized for the state to operate in. The power is yours — use it.

title: Karl Organizing: In-kind Donations
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In-kind Donations] Someone wants to give us gear instead of cash. Is that helpful?

Hell yes, take the gear and put it to work immediately. If a comrade has a high-end printer, a PA system, or a van they aren't using, that's thousands of dollars we don't have to raise ourselves. Every physical asset we own is a tool for the struggle, so catalog it, maintain it, and make sure it's always ready for the next mobilization.

title: Karl Organizing: Community Fridge Startup
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Community Fridge Startup] Can you explain: how do I start a fridge in my neighborhood without it getting shut down immediately?

Here's the thing: Find a local business owner or a comrade with a porch and an outdoor outlet who doesn't give a damn about city ordinances. Buy a used fridge, paint it with bright colors so it's impossible to ignore, and plug it in right on the sidewalk. Don't ask for permission from the state; just keep it clean and organized so the neighbors see it as a lifeline rather than an eyesore. When we feed each other, we prove the bosses are obsolete.

title: Karl Organizing: Social Media Safety
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Social Media Safety] Is it okay to post photos of our actions online?

Only if you've blurred every single face and hidden any identifying tattoos or unique clothing. Don't do the pigs' investigative work for them by posting high-res evidence of our people taking a stand. Keep the focus on the message and the movement, not on providing a digital lineup for the state's prosecutors.

title: Karl Organizing: Secure Communication
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Secure Communication] A friend asked me: 'How should our defense group talk to each other during an emergency?' What do I tell them?

Look, Stop using SMS or Facebook groups immediately because those are open books for the state. Stick to Signal with disappearing messages turned on and verify the safety numbers of every comrade in your circle. During an actual action, keep the chatter strictly to facts—location, numbers, and movement. We keep each other safe by keeping our mouths shut and our data encrypted.

title: Karl Organizing: Security Culture
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Security Culture] A friend asked me: 'How do we keep our coalition safe from people trying to break us up?' What do I tell them?

Keep your sensitive planning to small, vetted groups and leave the public posturing for the rallies. Don't talk about illegal tactics on apps that the cops can read, and verify the identity of anyone who wants access to your data or money. Paranoia is a trap, but being smart about who knows what is just basic survival in a fight against people with infinite resources. No one is coming to save us. That's the point.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, resource Pooling
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, resource Pooling] How do we fund these defense efforts without a big organization?

Start a community chest where everyone chips in a few bucks a month based on what they can afford. Use that money for bail, medical supplies, and cameras for the cop watch team. Keep the accounting transparent so everyone knows their money is going directly to the fight. We don't need billionaire grants when we have the collective power of our own pockets.

title: Karl Organizing: Enemy Counter-Fundraising
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Enemy Counter-Fundraising] Can you explain: how do we use our opposition to raise money?

Real talk: Nothing opens wallets faster than a common enemy. When a billionaire or a corrupt politician attacks your movement, use their own words to show your supporters why we're winning. Frame every contribution as a direct middle finger to the people trying to silence us, and watch the resources pour in from people who are fed up.

title: Karl Organizing: Dealing with consultants
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Dealing with consultants] Who are these 'labor relations specialists' the company just hired?

Look, Those are union-busting mercenaries paid thousands of dollars a day to lie to your face. Their only job is to spread fear, uncertainty, and doubt so you don't realize how much the boss is stealing from you. They get rich by keeping you poor. Tell your coworkers exactly what they're being paid and remind them that money could have gone into your paychecks instead.

title: Karl Organizing: Neighborhood Pods
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Neighborhood Pods] How many houses should be in one neighborhood pod to keep it manageable?

Keep it tight—ten to fifteen households is the sweet spot for actually knowing your neighbors' names and needs. If it gets too big, communication breaks down and people start feeling like a number again. You want a group where one person can walk to everyone else's front door in five minutes if the internet goes down. Once you hit twenty houses, it's time to split and help the next block start their own pod. Now go organize.

title: Karl Organizing: The 'Third Party' lie
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[The 'Third Party' lie] My manager says the union is an 'outside interest' that doesn't know our business.

Look your manager in the eye and ask, 'Who is the union? Is it the guy in the suit you hired for $500 an hour, or is it me and my coworkers?' We are the union. We're the ones who do the work and make the profit. The only 'outsider' is the union-busting consultant the boss brought in to protect their power. We know the business better than anyone because we run it.

title: Karl Organizing: Dealing with Small Landlords
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Dealing with Small Landlords] My landlord is just a 'mom and pop' who says they're struggling too. Should I be nicer?

The 'mom and pop' label is a mask for the same exploitative relationship. If they're struggling, they can sell the building to the tenants; they shouldn't be balance-billing their life on your back. A small-scale parasite still lives off your paycheck while you deal with the broken boiler. Treat them like a business because that's exactly how they'll treat you when the rent is late.

title: Karl Organizing: Signature Gathering
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Signature Gathering] A friend asked me: 'How do we get on the ballot without a massive paid staff?' What do I tell them?

Here's how it works: You need a brigade of volunteers who believe in the cause enough to hit the pavement every single weekend. Set up at grocery stores, transit hubs, and public parks to meet people where they already are. Treat every signature as a conversation and a potential new recruit for the movement, not just a box to check. We don't need consultants when we have a disciplined crew of comrades who know how to ask a neighbor for two minutes of their time.

title: Karl Organizing: Zines and DIY Media
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Zines and DIY Media] Can you explain: can selling zines actually help our budget?

Real talk: Zines are the classic way to fund the fight while spreading the word. They're cheap to produce and people love to hold something real in their hands. If you put out a high-quality, punchy zine every quarter, you're creating a recurring revenue stream that also educates your base on the front lines.

title: Karl Organizing: Sustaining the Fight
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Sustaining the Fight] Can you explain: how do we keep people from burning out on rapid response?

Rotate your shifts and make sure nobody is on call 24/7 or they'll be useless within a month. Celebrate your wins, no matter how small, and make time for communal meals and joy that have nothing to do with the pigs. This is a marathon, not a sprint, and we need every comrade healthy and sharp for the long haul. Rest is a radical act when the state wants you exhausted.

title: Karl Organizing: Verification
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Verification] How do we avoid acting on fake reports of police activity?

Look, Never share a report you haven't personally verified or heard from a trusted scout on the ground. Use a 'trusted source' protocol where two different people have to confirm the sighting before the alert goes out to the whole network. False alarms burn people out and make the network look unreliable. Slow is smooth, and smooth is fast when it comes to reporting state violence.

title: Karl Organizing: Burner Devices
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Burner Devices] A friend asked me: 'Can I just swap the SIM card in my regular phone to stay anonymous?' What do I tell them?

No. Your phone has a unique hardware ID called an IMEI that stays the same no matter what SIM you slide in. The network sees that 'Phone A' is now using 'SIM B' and links them instantly. If you need to be anonymous, you need a completely separate device that has never touched your personal life. Physical separation is the only real digital separation. No one is coming to save us. That's the point.

title: Karl Organizing: Public Messaging
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Public Messaging] Can you explain: how do we talk to the public so they actually care about our coalition?

Cut the academic jargon and speak directly to people's empty pockets and rising bills. Your message needs to be simple enough to fit on a cardboard sign and bold enough to make a landlord nervous. Use words that sound like a gut punch to the ruling class, not a sociology thesis; people want to know how you're going to help them win.

title: Karl Organizing: Sustainer Programs
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Sustainer Programs] A friend asked me: 'Is it better to ask for one big check or small monthly amounts?' What do I tell them?

Give me ten comrades chipping in ten bucks a month over one guy writing a thousand-dollar check any day of the week. Monthly sustainers provide the predictable floor we need to plan long-term campaigns without panicking about the rent. It builds a base of people who are spiritually and financially committed to the long haul, not just a one-time thrill. That's how we win.

title: Karl Organizing: Street Medics
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Street Medics] A friend asked me: 'What basic supplies should we have for community defense?' What do I tell them?

Every defense team needs a dedicated medic with a kit containing gauze, saline, gloves, and antacids for pepper spray. Don't just buy gear; get trained on how to use it so you aren't a liability when things go sideways. Keep your kit organized and your head on a swivel. We take care of our own because the system would rather see us bleed out on the sidewalk. Now go organize.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: secure Document Sharing
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: secure Document Sharing] Give me the short version: How can I send sensitive files to my organizing committee safely?

Real talk: Stop using Google Drive or Dropbox; those companies are just extensions of the state surveillance machine. Use OnionShare or a password-protected, encrypted zip file sent through an end-to-end encrypted channel. If the document is truly dangerous, put it on a thumb drive and hand it over in person. Digital trails are permanent; physical hand-offs are much harder to intercept.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, police Budgets
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, police Budgets] How do I talk about 'defunding' without losing the moderate vote?

Talk about 'investment' in the things that actually keep us safe: housing, healthcare, and youth programs. Point out that the police budget grows every year while the libraries close and the potholes stay empty. Ask your neighbors if they feel safer now than they did five years ago despite all that spending. We’re not just talking about taking money away; we’re talking about finally spending it on the people's actual needs.

title: Karl Organizing: De-escalation
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[De-escalation] What do I do if some guy starts screaming in my face while we're marching?

Let me break it down: Keep your cool and do not let their bait pull you into a cage. Use your body to create a physical barrier between the agitator and the rest of the march, and move the targeted comrade to the center of the group. If you engage, keep your voice low and steady, because their goal is to cause a scene that justifies a police crackdown while the ruling class watches and laughs.

title: Karl Organizing: Direct action
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Direct action] What is a 'march on the boss'?

Let me break it down: It's when the whole crew walks into the manager's office together to hand over a list of demands or your union petition. You don't send one representative; you all go. It shows the boss that they can't just bully one person into silence. Seeing the boss's face turn pale when fifty workers walk in at once is a massive boost to morale and proves who really runs the place.

title: Karl Organizing: Escalation Management
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Escalation Management] A friend asked me: 'What if the police get aggressive while we are watching them?' What do I tell them?

Hold your ground but don't give them an easy excuse to start swinging or shooting. Keep your cameras high and clearly state that you are peacefully observing. If they move in, back up slowly as a group, keeping your eyes on them the whole time. The goal is to survive to share the footage and keep the focus on their misconduct, not to end up in a hospital bed. Now go organize.

title: Karl Organizing: Power Mapping
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Power Mapping] How do we know which politician or CEO to target first?

Map out who actually signs the checks or passes the laws, then find out who those people are actually afraid of. Don't just protest into the void; find the specific person—the landlord, the CEO, the Council Chair—who has the power to give you what you want right now. Once you find that pressure point, you squeeze together as a coalition until they crack under the weight.

title: Karl Organizing: Rapid Response Setup
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Rapid Response Setup] How do I start a network to stop raids in my area?

Grab five friends you trust and get on an encrypted app like Signal right now. Map out your blocks and assign roles—scouts to spot the vans, legal observers, and phone-tree captains. When a raid starts, you don't panic; you flood the street with bodies and cameras to make the state's dirty work impossible. It's about being faster and more organized than the guys in tactical vests. Now go organize.

title: Karl Organizing: Intervention Ethics
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Intervention Ethics] Can you explain: when should I actually step in if I see a cop harassing someone?

Assess the situation and ask the person being harassed if they want help before you dive in. If they say yes, start filming and ask the officer for their name and badge number while standing at a safe distance. Sometimes just having three or four people watching silently with phones out is enough to make a bully in uniform back off. Solidarity means following the lead of the person in the crosshairs.

title: Karl Organizing: House Parties
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[House Parties] Can you explain: how do we make a house party fundraiser actually successful?

Keep the speeches short and the energy high. You want people to feel the heat of the movement, not sit through a boring lecture. Have a clear, bold 'ask' halfway through the night, pass a physical bucket, and make sure everyone knows exactly what fight that money is going toward before the music starts back up.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: labor Endorsements
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: labor Endorsements] Give me the short version: How do I get unions to back a radical campaign?

Here's how it works: Show up on their picket lines long before you ask for their vote. Talk to the rank-and-file workers, not just the leadership, and prove you understand their specific grievances. Be the candidate who explicitly supports the right to strike and the expansion of collective bargaining. If you want the muscle of organized labor behind you, you have to be the most reliable ally they’ve ever seen in public office.

No. Apple has the keys and they will hand them over. Use an encrypted note-taking app like Standard Notes or just keep them in an encrypted local file. If it’s in the cloud, it’s on someone else’s computer, and that someone else is a billionaire who doesn't care about your revolution. Keep your plans on hardware you control.

title: Karl Organizing: Decision Making
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Decision Making] A friend asked me: 'How do we make decisions without spending hours arguing over every detail?' What do I tell them?

Use a '70% agreement' rule for the big stuff and delegate the small stuff to specialized working groups. You don't need a full assembly to decide what color the flyers are; you need a few trusted comrades to just get it done. If you try to reach perfect consensus on everything, the billionaires will have bought another yacht before you've even picked a meeting spot. The power is yours — use it.

title: Karl Organizing: Canvassing tips
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Canvassing tips] How do I canvass effectively?

Listen more than you talk. The first 30 seconds decide everything — introduce yourself, name one local issue, ask what THEY care about. Don't argue with hostile doors; thank them and move on. Track every conversation. And bring water, comfortable shoes, and a buddy. Canvassing is a marathon, not a sprint.

title: Karl Organizing: Merch Strategy
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Merch Strategy] What kind of merch actually makes money for the movement?

Forget the cheap plastic trinkets that end up in a landfill. Print bold, defiant designs on union-made shirts or screen-print patches that comrades can sew onto their own gear to show their colors. Sell items that serve a purpose, like heavy-duty water bottles or thick canvas bags, and make sure every cent above cost goes toward organizing the next action. Now go organize.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: identifying Undercovers
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: identifying Undercovers] Give me the short version: How can we tell if someone at our meeting is an infiltrator?

Look, Watch for the person who pushes for illegal or violent action way too early or asks too many questions about people's private lives. Real comrades focus on the work and build trust over time through small, consistent actions. Don't get paranoid, but keep sensitive info on a need-to-know basis. If someone smells like a cop, they probably are; trust your gut and move the planning to a smaller circle.

title: Karl Organizing: Fundraising
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Fundraising] How can we get money for our movement without corporate sponsors?

Karl's answer: Host a backyard party or a community dinner where folks can chip in a few bucks for the cause. Use peer-to-peer apps to pool resources from the people who actually benefit from your work. Avoid the big non-profit grants that come with strings and keep the power in the hands of the working class.

title: Karl Organizing: Legal Rights Training
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Legal Rights Training] A friend asked me: 'What's the most important thing to teach neighbors about their rights?' What do I tell them?

The most powerful words anyone can say are 'I am remaining silent and I want a lawyer.' Teach everyone that the police are allowed to lie to you, so you should never believe a word they say during an interrogation. Run 'Know Your Rights' workshops in living rooms and parks until every kid on the block knows how to handle a stop. Knowledge is the first line of defense against the precinct. Start today.

title: Karl Organizing: Social Media OPSEC
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Social Media OPSEC] Can you explain: is it okay to tag my friends in photos from the community garden?

Here's the thing: Never tag anyone in any political context without their explicit, enthusiastic consent. Tagging creates a digital map of our networks for the state to study. Even a 'wholesome' garden project can be used to build a profile on organizers. Let people manage their own digital footprint; don't do the feds' job for them by building their database.

title: Karl Organizing: Escalation Management
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:

Hold your ground but don't give them an easy excuse to start swinging or shooting. Keep your cameras high and clearly state that you are peacefully observing. title: Karl Organizing: Skill-sharing for Cash
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Skill-sharing for Cash] A friend asked me: 'How can we raise money using our own talents?' What do I tell them?

Turn your movement into a school for the working class. Have your tech-savvy comrades run a workshop on digital security or your gardeners teach urban farming for a suggested sliding-scale fee. You're building the community's capacity and filling the treasury at the same time, which is a hell of a lot better than selling overpriced cookies. The power is yours — use it.

title: Karl Organizing: Quick advice: donor Capture
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Quick advice: donor Capture] Give me the short version: A wealthy businessman wants to give us a large sum but has some 'suggestions' on our messaging. Should we take it?

Tell him to keep his blood money and his opinions. The second you let a fat cat dictate your slogans is the second you stop being a threat to his class. If he wants to help, he can drop the cash in the bucket and walk away with no strings attached; otherwise, he's just buying a leash to put on your movement. The power is yours — use it.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, avoiding Sectarianism
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, avoiding Sectarianism] There is a group we have beef with, but they agree with us on this campaign. Do we work with them?

Let me break it down: I don't care if you hate their stickers or their favorite dead theorist. If they are willing to put boots on the pavement to stop an eviction or challenge a billionaire, they are a temporary comrade. Keep the internal beef for the pub and keep your eyes on the ruling class's throat; we don't have the luxury of purity tests when the rent is due.

title: Karl Organizing: In simple terms, crowdfunding Platforms
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[In simple terms, crowdfunding Platforms] Which website should we use to raise money online?

Avoid the big corporate platforms that take a massive cut and can freeze your funds the moment a right-wing rag complains. Look for worker-owned cooperatives or movement-aligned tech that prioritizes security and low fees. Better yet, set up a direct portal on your own site so the vultures don't get a single penny of the community's support.

title: Karl Organizing: Handling NGOs
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Handling NGOs] Can you explain: what do we do about non-profits that try to take over our coalition?

Use their office space, their lawyers, and their mailing lists, but never let them dictate your strategy to satisfy their board of directors. Keep the decision-making power in the hands of the workers and tenants who have everything to lose, not the careerists with a five-year 'advocacy' plan. If they try to tone down your demands to stay 'respectable,' thank them for the snacks and keep moving forward without them. That's how we win.

title: Karl Organizing: Phone Hygiene
author: MTCSTW Training Pack
text:
[Phone Hygiene] What should I do if a cop tries to take my phone?

Lock it instantly. On most modern phones, hitting the power button five times or holding the volume and power buttons will trigger a lockdown that requires a passcode to reopen. Don't say a word, don't give up the code, and demand a lawyer. Your data is the collective memory of our movement; don't let them pillage it because you were too slow to hit the lock. No one is coming to save us. That's the point.
